method.name: milp_workforce_production
steps: Define sets: weeks t=1..8, worker types (skilled/training/trained), product types (I/II)

Define parameters: demand_I[t], demand_II[t], hourly output (10 for I, 6 for II), wages (skilled=360, trainee_during=120, trainee_after=240, overtime=540), penalty rates (0.5 for I, 0.6 for II), initial skilled workers=50, training capacity per 2 weeks=3, target trainees=50

Decision variables: train[t]=# skilled workers training in week t (integer), ot[t]=# skilled workers on overtime in week t (integer), prod_I[t]=hours for food I (continuous), prod_II[t]=hours for food II (continuous), backlog_I[t]=kg backlog for food I at end of week t (continuous), backlog_II[t]=kg backlog for food II at end of week t (continuous), trained_inflow[t]=# new trainees starting training in week t (integer), trained_active[t]=# trained workers active in week t (integer)
Capacity constraint: prod_I[t]/10 + prod_II[t]/6 <= 40*(50 - train[t] - ot[t]) + 60*ot[t] + 40*trained_active[t] for all t
Overtime limit: ot[t] <= 50 - train[t] for all t
Training flow: trained_active[t] = sum(s=1..max(1,t-2), trained_inflow[s]) for t>=1 (workers active 2 weeks after starting training)
Training capacity: sum over any consecutive 2 weeks of train[t] <= 3*50 (each skilled can train max 3 over 2 weeks)
Training target: sum(t, trained_inflow[t]) = 50 (exactly 50 trainees by end of week 8)
Demand balance for I: backlog_I[t-1] + prod_I[t]/10 - backlog_I[t] = demand_I[t] for all t
Demand balance for II: backlog_II[t-1] + prod_II[t]/6 - backlog_II[t] = demand_II[t] for all t
Wage cost: 360*sum(t, 50-train[t]-ot[t]) + 540*sum(t, ot[t]) + 120*sum(t, trained_inflow[t]+trained_inflow[max(1,t-1)]) + 240*sum(t, trained_active[t])
Penalty cost: 0.5*sum(t, backlog_I[t]) + 0.6*sum(t, backlog_II[t])
Minimize total wage cost + penalty cost
All variables >= 0, train/ot/trained_inflow/trained_active integer

method.name: milp_aggregate_production
steps: Same sets and parameters as milp_workforce_production
Simplified training model: instead of tracking individual trainee flow, use cumulative count of active trained workers
trained_active[t] = sum(s=1..max(1,t-2), train[s]) for t>=1 (all who started training 2+ weeks ago are active)
Same capacity, overtime, demand balance, and cost structure as milp_workforce_production
Training capacity: sum over any consecutive 2 weeks of train[t] <= 3*50
Training target: sum(t, train[t]) = 50 exactly
Fewer integer variables - production variables are continuous
Minimize wage cost + penalty cost

method.name: milp_binary_week_selection
steps: Same sets and parameters as milp_workforce_production
Add binary variables: u[t] = 1 if any training in week t, v[t] = 1 if overtime in week t
train[t] <= 50*u[t], ot[t] <= 50*v[t]
Same production, backlog, training flow as milp_workforce_production
Same training capacity and target constraints
Same wage and penalty costs
More binary variables but captures discrete nature of training/overtime decisions better
Minimize total cost
